quotes.text: Computer use moves the AI from talking about work to doing the work, literally moving the cursor across the screen. It's slow, it's occasionally clumsy, but it's historic.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures in one line what makes computer use different from earlier Copilot features.

quotes.text: The AI doesn't memorize keystrokes. It understands goals. It assessed that manual typing would solve what clicking couldn't. That's autonomous reasoning.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the difference between agentic behavior and scripted macros.

quotes.text: The moment you enable computer use, your copilot agent doesn't just borrow your mouse. It borrows your authority.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints the core governance risk of desktop-acting agents.

quotes.text: If you'd revoke an employee's access during off boarding, you should also deactivate the agent's credentials. Otherwise you've built the world's first immortal contractor
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete lifecycle rule for agent identities with a memorable image.

quotes.text: Give your agent only the access it needs to complete its assigned task, nothing more, nothing adjacent. The temptation is to reuse the service account that already connects to everything. Resist it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear least-privilege recommendation for agent accounts.

takeaways: Computer use in Copilot Studio lets an agent operate a real Windows machine through vision and synthetic mouse and keyboard input, reaching apps that have no API or connector.
Setup requires Windows Pro or better, the Power Automate Desktop machine runtime, registration in the Power Automate portal and enabling the machine for computer use.
Treat each agent like a new employee: give it a scoped Entra Agent ID with least privilege, test in a sandbox, add human-in-the-loop approvals and monitor it with Purview and Defender.
hook: Copilot Studio can now click, type and open apps on a real Windows desktop. This episode is for Power Platform makers and IT security teams who want to automate legacy apps without APIs. See how computer use is set up, how the agent reasons through a Power App, and which governance guardrails keep it from becoming a teenager with root access.
